record.title: SkillGym reports agent training gains from executable human-workflow environments
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces SkillGym, a pipeline that turns human-written agent skills into executable tasks with code-based outcome checks and contrastive skill-dependence labels. The authors report 2,756 environments across 12 categories and 8,364 successful trajectories, then fine-tune Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on SkillGym trajectories. They report gains on GDPval-AA v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench, including performance that persists without inference-time skills. These remain paper-reported results. The paper’s v2 abstract and v2 HTML disagree on the no-skills SkillsBench gain (12.38 versus 14.68 points), and the reported benchmark comparisons depend on specific harnesses; code, dataset and model artifacts were not audited in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The v2 preprint describes SkillGym’s pipeline for converting human-written skills into executable environments with code-based outcome verifiers and reports 2,756 environments across 12 categories and 8,364 successful trajectories.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B improves GDPval-AA v2 by 199 Elo and Terminal-Bench 2.1 by 19.10 percentage points; the v2 HTML reports SkillsBench v1.1 gains of 28.13 points with skills and 14.68 without skills. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The arXiv v2 abstract reports a 12.38-point SkillsBench v1.1 gain without skills, while the v2 HTML body reports 14.68 points; the difference remains unresolved in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper distinguishes skill-dependent tasks, defined under a reference-agent contrastive test, from verifier-passed fallback tasks; it reports 1,081 skill-dependent and 1,675 verifier-passed environments. Across sampled tasks, 8,364 successful trajectories are reported at a 17.4% success rate.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper links code, environment/dataset and model artifacts, but those repositories and artifacts were not inspected in this review; task generators, verifier independence, data composition and training implementation remain unaudited.
No independent reproduction of the reported fine-tuning gains or cross-model comparisons was located in this bounded review.
The arXiv v2 abstract reports a 12.38-point SkillsBench v1.1 gain without skills while its v2 HTML body reports 14.68 points.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently reproducible, converting human-written workflows into executable, verifier-backed environments and training trajectories could materially expand procedural agent learning and long-horizon training data. A 7 reflects the scale of the released corpus and reported benchmark gains while limiting the claim to the paper’s evaluated tasks, models and harnesses; it is not a truth score.
limitations: Reported training and benchmark results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced in this review.
Benchmark comparisons depend on the model, harness and skill setting; the paper does not establish performance across arbitrary real-world workflows.
The paper reports 8,364 successful trajectories with a 17.4% sampled success rate; the trajectory corpus should not be interpreted as all attempted runs or universal task coverage.
Skill-dependent labels establish contrastive outcomes under a reference configuration, not that the skill is necessary for every model or harness.
The v2 abstract and v2 HTML disagree on the SkillsBench no-skills gain (12.38 versus 14.68 percentage points); unresolved here.
Code, dataset and model artifacts were not inspected during this review.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces SkillGym, a pipeline that turns human-written agent skills into executable tasks with code-based outcome checks and contrastive skill-dependence labels. The authors report 2,756 environments across 12 categories and 8,364 successful trajectories, then fine-tune Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on SkillGym trajectories. They report gains on GDPval-AA v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench, including performance that persists without inference-time skills. These remain paper-reported results. The paper’s v2 abstract and v2 HTML disagree on the no-skills SkillsBench gain (12.38 versus 14.68 points), and the reported benchmark comparisons depend on specific harnesses; code, dataset and model artifacts were not audited in this review.

technical.claimed_result: The v2 paper reports Qwen3.5-35B-A3B fine-tuning gains of 199 Elo on GDPval-AA v2 and 19.10 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, plus 28.13 points on SkillsBench v1.1 with skills and 14.68 without skills in the v2 HTML. The v2 abstract instead states 12.38 points for the no-skills condition. These values are author-reported.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports a large collection and multiple model/harness runs, but this review did not establish comparable dollar, energy or end-to-end training costs.
technical.demonstrated_result: The v2 preprint describes a skill-to-task construction pipeline and reports 2,756 environments and 8,364 successful trajectories; this review did not audit the releases or independently validate the counts.
technical.implementation_status: The paper lists GitHub and Hugging Face artifact links, but availability and contents were not checked in this activation.
technical.mechanism: Human-authored skills are organized into skill cards, paired with manually constructed category templates, instantiated as Docker tasks, checked for feasibility and verifier-passed solutions, then assessed for reference-agent skill dependence using with-skill versus without-skill runs. Successful sampled trajectories provide SFT data; code-verified outcomes can support RL.
technical.novelty: The work operationalizes human-written procedures as executable, outcome-verifiable task environments and training trajectories, with a contrastive dependence label distinct from task verifier success.
technical.regime: The paper reports 2,756 environments spanning 12 categories and 63 subcategories, with training and evaluation across Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, multiple teacher models/harnesses, GDPval-AA v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench v1.1.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint and its linked artifact locations are identified, but artifacts were not inspected and no independent reproduction was performed. The versioned SkillsBench discrepancy needs resolution.
technical.strongest_baseline: The reported base-versus-fine-tuned Qwen3.5-35B-A3B comparison is the most directly relevant within-paper comparison; cross-model leaderboard comparisons are not independent matched implementations.

brief.title: SkillGym reports agent training gains from executable human-workflow environments
brief.why_it_matters: If the paper’s results hold, verifier-backed environments derived from human workflows could provide a reusable route from written procedures to agent training data and help test whether procedural competence transfers beyond prompt-time skill use. The paper reports a large resource and substantial benchmark gains, but its evaluation is author-run, results are not independently reproduced here, and a versioned SkillsBench figure is inconsistent.
